Matt, saw Windfall's $65M from Morgan Stanley and the AI Copilot and Market Insights launches.

Scaling a new product line that fast usually means more nonprofit accounts in play than the team can cover before new reps ramp, and that is where deals go cold. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Windfall off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress ~4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?

Matt, quick follow-up for Windfall.

After a raise and two product launches, the pipeline expectation on enterprise nonprofit climbs faster than headcount can. Most teams don't actually know how many meetings they need booked to hit the new number, so the gap shows up late in the quarter.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I'll walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings your segment needs to hit target, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Matt, last bit of proof for Windfall.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Windfall's reply rate likely compares to other data and intelligence companies. Want to hop on a quick call and I'll walk you through it?
